full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case giving rise to the Rule, in brief, are that the 1st party O.P. Zahir Ahmed filed a petition in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate Cox's Bazar under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the 2nd party-petit loners alleging that the disputed lands described in the schedule appended to the petition comprising an area of 11.95 acres belong to the 1st party O.P. and his relations and they have been in peaceful possession of the same. The 2nd party petitioners were threatening to dispossess them forcibly, for which the 1st party Zahir Ahmed filed the application under Sec. 144 Cr.P.C. The learned Sub-divisional Officer directed the Officer-in-Charge, Moiscal P. S. to enquire and report. On the basis of the police report, the learned Magistrate drew up proceedings under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure res-training both the parties from entering in the disputed lands. The petitioners filed Criminal Motion No. 539 of 1976 in the Court of Sessions Judge, Chittagong. Mr. M. U. Aimed, the learned Additional Sessions Jud.ge, Chittagong heard the Motion and rejected the same on the ground that the petitioners did not file the written statement in the proceedings. So the 2nd party petitioners were directed to file written statement in the proceedings. Thereafter, the 2nd party petitioners filed written statement in the proceedings claiming their right, title and interest in the disputed lands. They asserted that there was no apprehension of breach of peace. The 1st party O. P. Zahir Ahmed and his relations have no right, title and possession in the disputed lands.
